source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed electrical appliance safety checks

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
Continue by filling in basic information such as:
   - Date and time of the test
   - Name and contact information of the technician conducting the test
   - Location of the test (address)
3. Record the make, model, and serial number of each electrical appliance tested.
4. Inspect each appliance visually for obvious signs of damage or wear, noting any findings.
5. Perform a series of operational checks, including:
   - Power on and off functionality
   - Cable and plug examination
   - Fuse checks (if applicable)
6. Use an approved PAT (Portable Appliance Testing) device to conduct a formal test. Record the following:
   - Earth continuity test results
   - Insulation resistance test results
   - Protective conductor current test results (Class I appliances)
   - Touch current test results (if applicable)
7. Record the test results as PASS or FAIL accordingly.
8. For appliances that FAIL:
   - Take
